experiment_title: Per-model cost vs panel-% (v2 — controlled re-run with foreground dispatch + bigger stages)
platform: Claude Code, Max 20x subscription, macOS Darwin 24.6.0
key_finding: Subagent-based per-model isolation is structurally impossible for /usage2 attribution because subagent returns become parent cache_write_1h at Opus rates. Both Stage 1 (Haiku-targeted) and Stage 2 (Sonnet-targeted) ended up 97-98% Opus-dominated. H1 vs H2 cannot be tested with this protocol.

stages.label: v2 Stage 1 — 16 foreground Haiku Explore agents (4 sequential + 12 parallel)
stages.notes: Foreground dispatch worked (16 subagents visible in toolUseResult), but parent cache_write_1h ($13.10) dominated cost. Opus cache_write_1h = caching Haiku subagent returns into parent context for future replays. The intended Haiku dominance is unreachable through this protocol.

stages.label: v2 Stage 2 — 2 foreground Sonnet general-purpose agents (implemented Stage-1 findings)
shipped_value: Min-delta calibrate guards (slope_with_fallback function + per-pair guards)
Mode/doc parity (removed ghost summary-fast, added calibrate-account-scope/estimate/reset-calibration to both SKILL.md files + meter.py docstring)
calibrate output now sensible: week_all $11.85/pp (was $300/pp), week_sonnet $8.11/pp (was $260/pp)
stages.notes: Same structural problem as Stage 1. Sonnet subagents only attributed $0.06 of Sonnet tokens (mostly cache_read). Parent Opus dominated at $3.31. The real value of this stage is the bug fixes shipped to meter.py.

stages.label: v2 Stage 3 — Opus main-thread synthesis (writing this doc, syncing, committing)
stages.notes: Not measured in isolation since main-thread Opus IS the natural pattern; full session totals captured in final summary.

hypothesis_test.H1_null: Panel %s linear in API-equivalent dollars regardless of model.
hypothesis_test.H3_methodology: Subagent dispatch via Agent tool causes parent thread to absorb cost via cache_write_1h regardless of subagent model.
hypothesis_test.result: H3 holds robustly. H1 and H2 cannot be tested with this protocol.
hypothesis_test.explanation: When the Claude Code agent dispatches a foreground subagent, the subagent's return (multi-thousand-token markdown report) becomes the parent's cache_write_1h on the next turn at the parent's model rate (Opus). For Haiku stage: 16 subagents' returns generated ~1.3M cache_write_1h tokens × $10/M Opus = $13.10. The Haiku subagents themselves cost $0.49. Parent cache cost was 27× the subagent's own cost.
hypothesis_test.future_test_design: To test H1 vs H2, would need either (a) three separate CC sessions each running a different default model, (b) direct API access (not available on subscription), or (c) cross-session JSONL aggregation. Not feasible via single-orchestrator + subagent dispatch.

implied_caps_v2.confidence: low (1pp + 3pp samples, both Opus-dominated; large jitter)

comparison_to_v1.likely_cause: v1 was averaged across varied workload with moderate concurrent activity; v2 captures single-instance Opus-orchestration cost

fixes_shipped_v2: slope_from_reports per-pair guards: delta_pp >= 1, delta_dollars > 0, time_span_seconds >= 60
slope_with_fallback wrapper: auto-defers to account_scope_slopes when clean-N < 5 or panel-Δ < 5pp
cmd_calibrate displays fallback reason when used
Mode/doc parity: removed ghost summary-fast, added 3 missing modes
meter.py docstring synced to include new modes
methodology_limitations: Foreground subagent dispatch attributes per-spawn tokens correctly, but cannot isolate per-model COST because parent cache writes absorb the returns
Stage sizes still small (3pp and 1pp); panel 1pp resolution adds ~±50% noise
5h trailing-window back-edge erosion for samples >5min apart — trailing_7d proxy not reliable
Per-model isolation hypothesis (H2) untested; no protocol available given subscription constraints
